summary: Phase 5c-i-α — NIP-44 v2 peer-encryption primitive added to tapit-attest. encryptTo / decryptFrom over secp256k1 ECDH + HKDF-SHA256 + ChaCha20 + HMAC-SHA256, built on @noble primitives already in deps, 13 spec-shaped tests covering round-trip, fresh-nonce, third-party MAC failure, wrong-sender MAC failure, tampered-payload MAC failure, version-byte 0x02, empty/oversized/non-hex rejection, unicode, multi-chunk padding, wrong-version rejection, and symmetry. All eight gates green; pushed to branch only.

why.text: Phase 5c (the Mycelium remote channel through Nostr) needs encrypted messages between two wallets through relays that must see ciphertext only. tapit-attest had passphrase-based AES-GCM but no peer/public-key encryption. NIP-44 v2 is the Nostr-native peer-encryption scheme and the spec is small enough that adding it directly — using primitives already in tapit-attest's @noble deps — beats pulling nostr-tools (a much larger surface, more attack-area, more code we'd have to vouch for). Operator picked this option ('I want to go with your recommended version').

outcome.notes: Pushed to claude/compare-library-wallet-OW5FF as commit 1338264. NOT pushed to main — operator hasn't said the word for this cut. Next is 5c-i-β: the Nostr wire client in the wallet that consumes encryptTo/decryptFrom and ships an encrypted envelope through a relay.

uncertainty: Implementation follows the NIP-44 v2 spec text and round-trips/tampers correctly, but interop against the upstream NIP-44 v2 reference vectors should be cross-checked before the wallet ships encrypted messages to real third-party Nostr clients. Tests note this explicitly.
ripple: app-connections — will become the consumer of encryptTo/decryptFrom in 5c-i-β
tapit-attest itself — new public surface (encryptTo, decryptFrom)
next: Cut Phase 5c-i-β — minimal Nostr wire client in the wallet (websocket + JSON event publish/subscribe) wrapped behind a transport-agnostic interface, using the new tapit-attest NIP-44 primitive for envelope encryption.
